fields.h1: Build Manufacturing Workflow Automation for the Plant Floor
fields.hero_description: Build manufacturing workflow automation that sends machine stops and quality holds to the right person by your limits.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for a Manufacturing Plant
fields.features_subheading: Each part covers one handoff between the floor and the people who support it, and every record ties back to a line or a lot.
fields.feature_1:
A stop clock on every machine

Operators log a stop from a tablet at the machine and pick a reason from your list. You choose how many minutes pass before the maintenance lead gets a direct message.
fields.feature_2:
Lots held by their reject rate

Inspectors enter the sample size and the count of failed parts. The app works out the reject rate and holds any lot over your limit, with photos sent to the quality manager.
fields.feature_3:
Engineering changes routed by cost

An engineer files a change with tooling and fixture costs on separate lines. Any change above your dollar limit goes to the plant manager before the drawing is released.
fields.feature_4:
AI reads incoming material certificates

An AI step pulls the heat number and test values off each material certificate. A person checks any field the AI is unsure of before the material is cleared for use.
fields.feature_5:
One board for the whole plant

The dashboard lists open machine stops and held lots for every line. It refreshes as each report comes in from the floor, and the morning meeting opens on today's numbers.
fields.feature_6:
The plant app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of the plant app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Anyone can read how each hold and approval is stored and extend it like any other codebase.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Handoffs Where a Plant Loses Time
fields.tab_content_1:
Maintenance hears when a press is down 20 minutes

Press 4 at Corvane Plastics stops with a jammed mold. Operator Teodric Vashti logs the stop from the tablet at the press and picks mold jam as the reason. Any stop longer than 20 minutes goes to the maintenance lead. The press has now been down 35 minutes, and Marisol Okonjo has a direct message naming it.
fields.tab_content_2:
When 7 of 200 brackets fail, the lot goes on hold

Lioba Farrant, an inspector at Dunmere Metalworks, pulls 200 brackets from lot 4471 and finds 7 with burrs on the punched edge. Any lot with more than 2% rejects goes on hold, and 7 of 200 is over that line. Osric Pellham, the quality manager, gets the lot record by email with 3 photos attached.
fields.tab_content_3:
Before release, ECR-112 needs the plant manager

Halvard Inoue at Kestrow Fabrication submits ECR-112 to move two holes on a mounting bracket: $6,200 in tooling and $4,900 for a new fixture, $11,100 in all. Production and quality have signed. A change over $10,000 also needs the plant manager, Yevgenia Thorsby, before the drawing is released.
fields.tab_content_4:
After a shift 160 cases short, Line 2 is reviewed

Renske Abernathy, shift lead at Altamore Foods, files the second-shift report for Line 2 from her phone. The line packed 1,840 cases against a 2,000-case plan, 160 short. She logs a 40-minute labeler fault as the cause. Any shift under 95% of plan goes to the production manager, Caius Wendroth, by direct message.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps from a list of plant handoffs to manufacturing workflow automation running on every line, built with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Map where work waits on the floor
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put a number on every rule
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the plant app in one prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Connect the systems you already run
fields.howto_step_1_des: Walk one line from start to finish and note each point where work waits on a person, such as a stopped machine waiting for maintenance or a lot waiting for an inspector. Write the owner of each wait beside it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide the number each rule runs on. Pick how many minutes a machine can sit stopped before maintenance hears, and which reject rate puts a lot on hold. Then set the dollar amount at which an engineering change needs the plant manager.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write one prompt that names each record and the rule it follows, such as a lot that goes on hold above 2% rejects. Emergent builds the app and its database from your prompt, and a later prompt changes either one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect your ERP or production system through its API, and work orders and part numbers arrive without retyping. Add Slack or email for the alerts, and name the person who receives each one instead of posting to a shared channel.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Fit the floor screens to the floor
fields.howto_step_5_des: Open each screen on the tablet or phone your operators carry and keep it to what someone can enter in under a minute. Offer stop reasons and defect types as a short list to tap, not a text box to type into.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Run one line on the app first
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give one line 2 weeks on the app alongside your current paper or spreadsheet process. Compare what the app flagged with what supervisors caught by hand, and move a limit wherever the two lists disagree.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Add lines one at a time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Add the next line once the first runs clean, and give it its own limits where its machines or parts differ. Review the plant board in the weekly operations meeting, and give every open stop and held lot an owner.

faq_plan.a: Manufacturing workflow automation is software that moves a plant's records between the floor and the teams that support it, by rules you set. It sends each machine stop, inspection result, change request, and shift report to the person who acts on it, and alerts someone when an item passes its limit.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up manufacturing workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Pick one line and the record it raises most, such as machine stops, and write down the limit that should trigger action, like 20 minutes down. In Emergent's AI automation builder, you describe those records and limits in a prompt and get a working app with its database.

faq_plan.q: Which plant handoff should manufacturing workflow automation start with?
faq_plan.a: Start with the handoff where work waits longest for a person. Pull a month of machine stops and held lots, and add up the hours each type sat before someone acted. The type with the most waiting hours goes first. Leave reviews that happen once a quarter on email for now.

faq_plan.q: Can manufacturing workflow automation track installation jobs at a customer site?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each installation a job record tied to the order it came from, with the install date and a checklist the installer completes on a phone. A missed date or a failed check alerts the person who owns the job. When installs run like building projects, with RFIs and daily logs, construction workflow automation covers that side.

faq_plan.q: How do operators log machine downtime in manufacturing workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Log it at the machine in two taps: one to start the stop and one to pick the reason. Keep the reason list under 10 items, drawn from the causes your maintenance team already tracks, and let the app record when the stop starts and ends. Make typed notes optional.

faq_plan.q: Can manufacturing workflow automation connect to an ERP system?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the ERP offers an API. Apps built with Emergent connect to any tool that has an API, pulling data in and sending it back out. Work orders and part numbers can come in from the ERP, and finished counts or held lots can go back to it without anyone keying a shift report twice.

faq_plan.q: Can manufacturing workflow automation request spare parts when a machine breaks?
faq_plan.a: Yes. When maintenance closes a stop with a broken part as the cause, the app can open a spare part request tied to that machine and that stop. The request then needs a price and an approver, and that request-to-order path is procurement automation, which can read the same machine record.

faq_plan.q: How do I know if manufacturing workflow automation is saving time?
faq_plan.a: Measure how long work waits, not how many clicks it takes. Before you switch, note the average wait for maintenance after a machine stop and the average wait for a decision on a held lot. After a month on the app, compare the same two averages using the timestamps on each record.

faq_plan.q: Do shop floor workers need training for manufacturing workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Only a short walkthrough, as long as each screen asks for one thing at a time. Show operators the stop screen at the start of a shift and have each one log a test stop. If a screen confuses people, Emergent changes it when you prompt again.

faq_plan.q: Can manufacturing workflow automation track supplier quality over time?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Save every inspection result against the supplier who shipped the lot, and the app can show each supplier's lots received and lots rejected by month. That inspection history stays in a database you own. Onboarding suppliers and renewing their contracts belongs to a vendor management workflow.
